Account for incompleteness; focus on structural decisions that are hard to reverse later.

I have all the evidence needed. Let me now compile findings:

1. `JobOutputStatsBar` receives `statusCounts` as a prop but ignores it entirely — it reads `hardCodedStatsCounts` everywhere.
2. `appliedFilters` object is reconstructed on every render and then immediately used as a `useMemo` dependency — the memo never achieves stability.
3. The columns-to-search dropdown shows `columnsToHide.options` but has a TODO comment noting it should use `colsToSearch` — the button's tooltip also says "Select columns to search", so this wires the wrong data.
4. `PreviewJobOutputTitle` takes both `options/setOptions` AND deeply nested `actions.fabOptions` + `actions.search` + `filters.*`, while also re-implementing `appliedFilters` logic internally — the title is acting as a second state coordinator for the modal's filter state.
5. `ToolbarFilter` generic: the `FullSelectOptions extends boolean` discriminant is non-standard and the default for `Value` is `Option` (single), but `columnsToSearch` and `columnsToHide` are declared with `Value = string[]` — fine, but the `SetState<Value>` type for `onChange` forces the caller to handle the full setState signature even for simple callbacks.
6. Debug `console.log` in `use-job-output.ts` line 176.

findings.title: JobOutputStatsBar ignores its statusCounts prop and renders hardcoded fixture data
findings.problem: The component signature accepts `statusCounts: StatusCounts` as a prop, but every computation inside the component body reads `hardCodedStatsCounts` instead. `allCount` (line 58), `groupedCounts` (line 60), and every bar segment width and tooltip value all use the fixture. The live prop is entirely unused. When this component is used in the real modal the bar will always display the same made-up numbers regardless of the actual job's row breakdown.
findings.suggestion: Replace all reads of `hardCodedStatsCounts` with the prop argument. `StatusCounts` includes an `all` key so `allCount` should be `statusCounts.all`. The helper `getGroupedStatusCounts` expects `StatusCounts<true>` (no `all` key) so either destructure `all` out before passing or adjust the helper's signature to accept the broader type.
findings.incompleteness_caveat: The hardcoded values may be intentional scaffolding while the visual design is being finalized, but the prop is already passed from the parent (preview-job-modal.title.tsx line 462), so this is a wiring omission rather than a placeholder, and it will silently display wrong data when the modal ships.

findings.title: appliedFilters constructed inline defeats useMemo: the memo recomputes every render
findings.problem: The `appliedFilters` record is a plain object literal created inside the render function body on lines 109-152. It is then passed as the sole dependency of `useMemo` on line 158. Because the object has a new reference on every render, the memo dependency check always fails and `appliedFilterState` is recomputed unconditionally on every render of `PreviewJobOutputTitle`. The same render-instability means the React Compiler cannot lift it either, since its contents reference props and options directly. The title re-renders on search keystrokes (search value changes), sheet tab clicks, and status filter changes, so this is a hot path.
findings.suggestion: Either inline `appliedFilterState` directly from a `useMemo` whose deps are the individual values the filters read from (e.g. `actions.search.value`, `filters.status.value`, `options.showFabOptions`, etc.), or extract `appliedFilters` to a stable `useMemo` first and then derive `appliedFilterState` from it in a separate memo. The former is simpler given the React Compiler is enabled for this project.

findings.title: Columns-to-search dropdown wired to the wrong filter options
findings.problem: The `Dropdown` inside the search input's `after` slot renders `filters.columnsToHide.options` (line 187) and its button tooltip reads 'Select columns to search'. The TODO comment on line 185 confirms this is wrong: it should feed `filters.columnsToSearch`. Because both options lists are sourced from `nonActionHeaders` in the parent, the values happen to be the same string array, masking the bug visually. But the `onChange` callback is never wired at all (the DropdownMenu has no selection handler), so clicking a column in this dropdown does nothing. When the two lists diverge or the onChange is wired, it will still update the wrong filter.
findings.suggestion: Swap `filters.columnsToHide.options` to `filters.columnsToSearch.options` and wire the `onChange` of the DropdownMenu to `filters.columnsToSearch.onChange`. Consider using a `SearchSelectV2` (as is done for the columnsToHide filter below) rather than a bare `DropdownMenu` so selection state is reflected visually.
findings.incompleteness_caveat: The TODO comment and missing onChange handler make it clear this control is intentionally unfinished. The finding stands because the wrong prop is already referenced by name, which will cause a silent misbehavior when the handler is wired.

findings.title: Title component holds appliedFilters logic that belongs in the modal or a dedicated hook
findings.problem: The title component receives the raw filter state from the modal parent via `filters`, `actions`, and `options`, then re-derives a second representation of the same state inside itself as `appliedFilters` and `appliedFilterState` (lines 109-157). It owns a full `AppliedFilter<T>` type definition and a `label` / `active` / `Icon` per-filter specification. This means filter display logic is split across two files: the modal owns filter state and the title owns filter labelling. When a new filter is added to the modal the title also needs editing. The title is acting as a partial state-coordinator rather than a pure layout shell.
findings.suggestion: Move the `appliedFilters` map and the `AppliedFilter` type to the modal (or a `useAppliedFilters` hook co-located with `useJobOutput`). Derive `appliedFilterState` there and pass only the resolved display list down to the title as a single prop. The title then becomes: receive display list, render chips. This also eliminates the unstable `useMemo` dependency issue above.

findings.title: ToolbarFilter SetState<Value> type forces unnecessary setter overload on simple callbacks
findings.problem: The `onChange` field of `ToolbarFilter` is typed as `SetState<Value>` which is React's `Dispatch<SetStateAction<Value>>` union (value | prev => value). All callers in both the modal and the title pass simple value callbacks, not updater functions. The `sheets` filter's `onChange` in the modal (line 325) wraps with `(val) => val && setTabToShow(val)` precisely to adapt a guarded write to the `SetState` signature. The type is technically correct but unnecessarily broad for a filter toolbar, making every callsite noisier.
findings.suggestion: Unless updater-function callbacks are needed, type `onChange` as `(value: Value) => void`. This is a one-line change to the type but makes all call sites cleaner and removes the need for the `val &&` guard wrapper.

findings.title: Debug console.log left in useJobOutput
findings.problem: `console.log('setTabToShow', metadata?.outputFileTabs?.[0])` inside the tab auto-select `useEffect` will fire in production whenever a multi-tab job output loads. It leaks internal state names and array contents to the browser console.
findings.incompleteness_caveat: Likely left in from development. Flagged only because it is in a data hook that will run for all users.

content.text:
Here is a summary of what was reviewed and why each finding matters.

**Files reviewed:**
- `/frontend/src/app/jobs/(list)/modals/preview-job-output.modal.tsx` — the modal and its state ownership
- `/frontend/src/app/jobs/(list)/modals/preview-job-output/preview-job-modal.title.tsx` — title/toolbar component and types
- `/frontend/src/app/jobs/(list)/modals/preview-job-output/job-status-bar.tsx` — status bar sub-component
- Supporting: `use-job-output.ts`, `status.ts`, `jobs.types.ts`

---

**High severity**

1. `JobOutputStatsBar` accepts `statusCounts` but reads `hardCodedStatsCounts` everywhere. The prop is passed from the parent and non-null, so this is a live wiring omission rather than a stub. The bar will display the same 10-item fixture for every job.

2. `appliedFilters` is a plain object literal in the render function body used as the only dep of `useMemo`. The memo fails its equality check on every render and recomputes unconditionally. This is the hot path since the title re-renders on every search keystroke.

**Medium severity**

3. The "columns to search" dropdown inside the search input `after` slot renders `filters.columnsToHide.options` instead of `filters.columnsToSearch.options`, and its `onChange` is not wired at all. The TODO comment on line 185 confirms the bug. Values look the same today only because both lists happen to come from the same `nonActionHeaders` array.

4. The title component re-derives `appliedFilters` (with `active`, `label`, `Icon` per filter) from the raw state it receives as props. This splits filter display logic across two files and makes the title a partial state coordinator rather than a display shell. Every new filter added to the modal requires a parallel edit in the title.

**Low severity**

5. `ToolbarFilter.onChange` is typed as `SetState<Value>` (i.e., `Dispatch<SetStateAction<Value>>`). All callsites pass simple value callbacks, not updater functions, and one callsite wraps with `val && setTabToShow(val)` specifically to adapt to the broader type.

6. `console.log("setTabToShow", ...)` left in `useJobOutput` at line 176 inside the tab auto-select effect.
